drafted_from: tool:github:gitroomhq-postiz-app's row in tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json (job, run, get_it, needs) and its sources row in sources.json; the command is the row's own run line with synthetic input filled in. start_here: Say to your AI: "Use Postiz on my computer: schedule and publish posts to your own social media accounts from one place you host yourself." It reads the row, installs Postiz if it is missing, runs it and shows you what it made.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list: Postiz is a program that runs on the person's own computer and works on what it is handed there.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Use Postiz on my computer: schedule and publish posts to your own social media accounts from one place you host yourself." It reads the row with do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools, method tools:list, input {tool: "tool:github:gitroomhq-postiz-app"}.
2. It checks that docker are on your computer, and if Postiz is missing it runs the get_it steps: git clone https://github.com/gitroomhq/postiz-app.git ; cd postiz-app ; docker compose up -d.
3. It runs the row's command: docker compose up -d
4. Read what it shows you and open the result. The site you asked through runs none of this; it all happens on your own computer.

worked_examples.title: Postiz: your own Postiz on your computer
worked_examples.ask: Use Postiz on my computer: schedule and publish posts to your own social media accounts from one place you host yourself.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/tools-from-github/tool-rows.json: tool:github:gitroomhq-postiz-app runs on your computer, so after tools:list the AI runs, in the folder it got Postiz in, the command line: docker compose up -d
worked_examples.hands_back: docker compose prints each container it starts (postiz, its Postgres and Redis) as Started; Postiz then answers in the browser at the address set in docker-compose.yaml, where you sign up as its first user and connect your social accounts.
